title: Engineering Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 for High-Yield Photosynthetic Biomanufacturing via CRISPR-dCas9 Dynamic Transcriptional Repression
target: Glycogen synthase (glgC) and competitive carbon sink pathways

matrix.yellow: Excess carbon diversion into competing intracellular storage glycogen (32% of fixed carbon)
matrix.green: Wild-type untreated Synechocystis PCC 6803 under identical photobioreactor conditions
matrix.citation: Kanno et al. (2024). Metabolic flux engineering in Synechocystis. Nat Chem Biol.

funnel.tier1: Global industrial decarbonization requires carbon-negative biological chemical production platforms to replace petroleum feedstocks.
funnel.tier2: Cyanobacteria fix carbon dioxide directly using sunlight with theoretical solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency exceeding 8%.
funnel.tier3: However, commercial viability is severely bottlenecked by metabolic slippage into native carbohydrate storage pathways under high light.
funnel.tier4: We hypothesize that inducible CRISPR-dCas9 repression of glycogen synthase (glgC) will redirect photosynthetic carbon flux into target terpenes by over 45% without compromising cell viability.

aims.aim1: Construct and validate light-inducible dCas9 repression cassettes targeting glgC in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803.
aims.aim2: Quantify metabolic carbon redirection and photosynthetic efficiency under continuous photobioreactor cultivation.
aims.aim3: Evaluate continuous production yield and genetic stability across 500 hours of continuous biomanufacturing.

control_triad.negative: Untransformed wild-type PCC 6803 and non-targeting dCas9 scramble guide control.
control_triad.positive: Constitutively active knockout mutant glgC::kanR strain under standard illumination.

aims_contingencies.aim1_fallback: If dCas9 off-target silencing occurs, switch to a high-fidelity dCas12a variant with orthogonal crRNA scaffolds.

usps: First light-switchable epigenetic carbon diverter in cyanobacteria operating without permanent genomic scar insertion.

biotech_risk_matrix.off_target: Off-target dCas9 binding to essential metabolic promoters
biotech_risk_matrix.metabolic_burden: Protein expression burden from high-copy repressor complexes
biotech_risk_matrix.regulatory_gmo: Horizontal gene transfer containment in photobioreactor closed loops

abstract: Photosynthetic biomanufacturing in cyanobacteria represents an attractive carbon-negative alternative to petrochemical synthesis. However, natural cyanobacteria divert over 30% of fixed solar carbon into intracellular glycogen storage, severely penalizing product yields. In this study, we engineer Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 using a light-inducible CRISPR-dCas9 transcriptional repression system targeting the glycogen biosynthesis gene glgC. By decoupling metabolic redirection from vegetative biomass accumulation, we achieve high-efficiency carbon shunting toward high-value biochemicals without triggering permanent growth defects. In photobioreactor cultivation, our dynamic repressor achieves a 48% reduction in storage carbohydrate accumulation with a concomitant 3.2-fold increase in target terpene flux relative to wild-type controls. Furthermore, stability audits over 500 hours confirm robust construct retention. This work establishes a generalizable, non-destructive regulatory paradigm for photosynthetic chassis engineering.

pillars.notes: Host chassis Synechocystis well-matched with dCas9 tool.
